note.explanation: The gradient of a speed-time graph tells us the average acceleration. Find it by dividing the change in speed by the time taken.
examples: If speed changes from 4 m s⁻¹ to 10 m s⁻¹ in 3 s, the gradient is (10 − 4)/3 = 2 m s⁻².
If speed stays constant, the speed-time graph is horizontal and its gradient is zero.
note.checkAnswer: The average acceleration is 2 m s⁻².
note.simple: A steeper speed-time graph means speed is changing more quickly. A flat graph means speed is not changing.
note.checkQuestion: A body's speed changes from 6 m s⁻¹ to 18 m s⁻¹ in 4 s. What is the gradient?
note.title: Gradient of a Speed-Time Graph
steps: Find the change in speed: 18 − 6 = 12 m s⁻¹.
Divide the change in speed by the time: 12/4 = 3 m s⁻².
State the gradient as 3 m s⁻².

options: The change in speed divided by the time taken
The distance covered divided by the time taken
The speed multiplied by the time taken
The change in time divided by the change in speed
mcqs.stem: What does the gradient of a speed-time graph represent?
rationales: This is correct because gradient is change in speed divided by the time taken, which gives average acceleration.
This is speed, not the gradient of a speed-time graph.
This product is not the gradient and does not give acceleration.
This reverses the ratio used to find the gradient.

mcqs.stem: What is the SI unit of the gradient of a speed-time graph?
rationales: m s⁻¹ is the unit of speed, not acceleration.
This is correct because dividing speed in m s⁻¹ by time in seconds gives m s⁻².
m is a unit of distance and is not the unit of a speed-time gradient.
s is a unit of time and is not the unit of a speed-time gradient.

options: The body has constant positive acceleration
mcqs.stem: A speed-time graph is a horizontal line above the time axis. What does this show?
rationales: This is correct because the speed does not change, so the gradient and acceleration are zero.
A horizontal graph has zero gradient, not constant positive acceleration.
A horizontal line above the time axis shows a non-zero, constant speed rather than rest.
The straight horizontal line does not show changing acceleration.

mcqs.stem: A straight speed-time graph rises steadily from left to right. What does it show?
rationales: This is correct because the rising straight line shows speed increasing at a constant rate.
A decreasing speed would be shown by a line falling from left to right.
A constant speed is represented by a horizontal line.
An object at rest has zero speed, represented by a line on the time axis.

mcqs.stem: A straight speed-time graph falls from left to right. What is the sign of its gradient?
rationales: A rising graph has a positive gradient, not a falling graph.
This is correct because speed decreases as time increases, so the graph has a negative gradient.
A zero gradient is shown by a horizontal graph.
The gradient can be found from the change in speed and the time taken.

mcqs.stem: A body's speed rises from 4 m s⁻¹ to 16 m s⁻¹ in 4 s. What is the gradient of its speed-time graph?
rationales: 6 m s⁻² is incorrect because the change in speed is 12 m s⁻¹ and must be divided by 4 s.
This is correct because (16 − 4)/4 = 3 m s⁻².
2 m s⁻¹ has the wrong unit and is not the change in speed divided by time.
12 m s⁻² is the numerical change in speed, but it has not been divided by the time.

options: The speed is constant and non-zero
mcqs.stem: A horizontal speed-time graph lies above the time axis. Which statement is correct?
rationales: A graph on the time axis would represent zero speed; this graph lies above it.
This is correct because the graph is horizontal, so speed is constant, and its height above the axis shows that speed is non-zero.
An increasing acceleration would require a changing gradient, not a horizontal line.
A speed-time graph shows speed and does not by itself show the direction of motion.

options: The speed-time graph has a constant gradient
The speed-time graph has zero speed throughout
mcqs.stem: A body moves with constant acceleration. What shape does its speed-time graph have?
rationales: This is correct because constant acceleration means the speed changes by equal amounts in equal time intervals, giving a constant gradient.
A horizontal graph shows constant speed and zero acceleration.
A vertical graph would not describe speed changing over time in this way.
Zero speed throughout means the body is at rest, not that it has constant acceleration.

examTips: A board question may ask what the gradient of a speed-time graph represents; state that it is average acceleration.
For a numerical gradient, show the change in speed, the time interval, and the division: (v₂ − v₁)/(t₂ − t₁).
Include the correct unit, m s⁻², when the speeds are in m s⁻¹ and time is in seconds.
For a graph interpretation, identify a rising line as positive acceleration, a falling line as negative gradient, and a horizontal line as zero acceleration.

The change in speed divided by time is the average acceleration.
Therefore, the gradient of the speed-time graph is equal to acceleration.

yourTurn.question: In Fig. 2.22, the speed at t₁ is the same as the speed at t₂. Find the slope of the speed-time graph.

steps.why: The textbook identifies the speeds at t₁ and t₂ as the same for this graph.
steps.text: The speed v₁ at time t₁ is the same as speed v₂ at time t₂, hence, the change in speed is also zero.

steps.why: Subtracting the equal speeds gives zero change in speed.
The slope is calculated by dividing the change in speed by the time interval.

example.question: For the speed-time graph in Fig. 2.22, find its slope.

explain.title: Finding the gradient
explain.body: The gradient is the change in speed divided by the time taken. In symbols, slope = (v₂ − v₁)/(t₂ − t₁) = Δv/t. The change in speed is the final speed minus the initial speed.

explain.title: Gradient means average acceleration
explain.body: Since average acceleration is the change in speed divided by time, the gradient of a speed-time graph is equal to the average acceleration of the body.

explain.title: Reading the graph shape
explain.body: A rising straight line shows that speed is increasing. A horizontal straight line shows that speed stays constant, so its gradient and the acceleration are zero.

explain.title: Constant acceleration
explain.body: When acceleration is constant, the speed-time graph is a straight line. The speed rises through the same amount for equal intervals of time.

mistakes: Do not divide time by the change in speed; use change in speed divided by time.
Do not confuse the gradient of a speed-time graph with the area under the graph.
A horizontal speed-time graph does not mean the body is at rest; it can show constant non-zero speed.
Do not leave out the unit of acceleration when giving a numerical gradient.
A negative gradient on a speed-time graph means speed is decreasing; it does not by itself tell you the direction of travel.
